title: Black Piranhas Bite With 30 Times Their Own Body Weight

scenes.text: Black piranhas bite with thirty times their own body weight.
Scientists caught fifteen of them in Brazil.
They measured each bite with a special force gauge.
The fish were only eight to fifteen inches long.
Their bite was nearly three times stronger than an alligator of the same size.
Their jaw muscles are huge for their size.
An extinct relative bit even harder. Thirty times their own weight, every bite.

description:
Black piranhas bite with thirty times their own body weight.
Scientists measured wild black piranhas in Brazil and found a bite nearly three times stronger than an alligator of the same size.
Would you swim with them?
first_comment: Bonus: an extinct relative, Megapiranha, may have bitten with up to about 1,000 pounds of force. Which animal should we test next?
